profile.intro: Brokers ask for it before opening an account, to offer you products that fit your horizon and how much risk you tolerate. Taking it here shows you what it is like and what it is for.
profile.notAdvice: Educational content. Your result is not a recommendation and never becomes a portfolio: it only helps you understand the questions you will be asked.

meaning.conservative: You put not losing what you invest first, even if it grows less. Brokers usually show low-risk, high-liquidity instruments first.
meaning.moderate: You look for a balance: you accept some ups and downs so your money can grow in the medium term.
meaning.aggressive: You tolerate sharp drops in search of more long-term growth. It still makes sense to invest only money you will not need soon.

SIM-3.short: How much your money buys with inflation, month by month.

SIM-1.title: Monthly budget
SIM-1.short: Your income, your expenses and what is left, against 50/30/20 or 70/20/10.
SIM-1.intro: Build your month and compare it with a reference rule. The rule is a starting point, not an obligation.

aguinaldo.label: Add the prorated aguinaldo
aguinaldo.help: The aguinaldo (13th-month salary) spread over 12 months, approximated as the net salary divided by 12.

needs.label: Spending on needs
needs.help: Rent, food, bills and transport. For example: 650.000

wants.label: Spending on wants
wants.help: Going out, clothes, subscriptions. For example: 186.500

rule.label: Reference rule
rule.help: 50/30/20 in general; 70/20/10 if your fixed expenses are high.

SIM-1.sentence: With this data, needs are {{needs}} of your income, wants {{wants}} and you have {{saved}} left to save. Compare it with the {{rule}} reference.
SIM-1.sentenceNegative: With this data, expenses exceed income by {{missing}}. Check which expense can be adjusted.
SIM-1.chartConclusion: Each bar compares your amount with what the {{rule}} rule suggests.
SIM-1.meaning: The 50/30/20 and 70/20/10 rules are starting points. If your needs go above the reference, it is not a mistake: it is information to decide where to adjust or how to save even a little each month.
SIM-1.try: Try switching the rule to 70/20/10 and see how the savings reference changes.
assumptions: One month of income and expenses, with no price changes.
The prorated aguinaldo is an approximation: monthly net divided by 12.
What is left after needs and wants counts as savings.

SIM-2.title: Emergency fund
SIM-2.short: How much you need, how much is missing and in how many months you get there.
SIM-2.intro: Calculate your emergency fund from your essential expenses and how many months it takes to build it.

essentials.label: Essential expenses per month
essentials.help: Rent, food, bills and transport. For example: 650.000

months.label: Months of coverage
months.help: 3 to 6 months is a common reference.

monthly.label: How much you set aside per month

SIM-2.sentence_one: You are missing {{missing}}. Setting aside {{monthly}} per month, you get there in {{count}} month.
SIM-2.sentence_other: You are missing {{missing}}. Setting aside {{monthly}} per month, you get there in {{count}} months.
SIM-2.sentenceNoSaving: You are missing {{missing}}. Without a monthly amount, there is no estimated date.
SIM-2.sentenceDone: You already reached your goal: keeping it available and risk-free is what matters now.
SIM-2.chartConclusion_one: At this pace, the savings line reaches the goal in {{count}} month.
SIM-2.chartConclusion_other: At this pace, the savings line reaches the goal in {{count}} months.
SIM-2.meaning: The emergency fund is for real surprises, like a health problem or losing your job. It is best kept available within 24 hours and risk-free.
SIM-2.try: Try changing the months of coverage from 3 to 6 and see how much longer it takes.
assumptions: Constant essential expenses.
Equal contributions every month, with no yield.
Months are rounded up: a partial month still requires saving.

SIM-4.title: Real rate
SIM-4.short: Whether a rate beats the scenario's inflation or not.
SIM-4.intro: Go from the nominal annual rate (TNA) to the rate for the period and compare it with inflation over the same period.

tna.label: Nominal annual rate (TNA)
tna.help: As an annual percentage, for example: 34

inflation.label: Scenario monthly inflation
inflation.help: As a monthly percentage, for example: 3

SIM-4.sentenceWins: Over {{days}} days, the period rate ({{rate}}) is above the period inflation ({{inflation}}): your money gains purchasing power in this scenario.
SIM-4.sentenceLoses: Over {{days}} days, the period rate ({{rate}}) does not reach the period inflation ({{inflation}}): your money loses purchasing power in this scenario.
SIM-4.meaning: The TNA is a reference rate; what you earn over a term is TNA × days ÷ 365. The real rate discounts inflation: if it is negative, the money buys less at the end even with more pesos.
SIM-4.try: Try changing inflation to the high scenario (6 %) and see what happens to the real rate.
assumptions: Constant monthly inflation over the period.
Simple interest for the term: TNA × days ÷ 365.
No taxes or fees.

SIM-5.title: Traditional or UVA term deposit
SIM-5.short: What is left in pesos and in purchasing power with each one.
SIM-5.intro: Compare a traditional term deposit with a UVA one (inflation-adjusted) in the same scenario.

tna.label: Traditional term deposit TNA
tna.help: As an annual percentage, for example: 34

uvaExtra.label: UVA additional rate
uvaExtra.help: As an annual percentage, for example: 1

inflation.label: Scenario monthly inflation
inflation.help: As a monthly percentage, for example: 3

SIM-5.tradHigher: The traditional one ends with more
SIM-5.sentence: After {{days}} days, the traditional one reaches {{trad}} and the UVA one {{uva}}, in this scenario.
SIM-5.pillMinimum: Many banks ask for 90 or 180 days for the UVA
SIM-5.chartTitle: Final amount in pesos and in purchasing power
SIM-5.chartConclusion: The second bar of each option discounts the scenario's inflation.
SIM-5.meaning: The traditional one pays a fixed rate; the UVA one adjusts the principal for inflation and adds a small rate. If inflation goes up, the UVA protects better; if it goes down, it can earn less. Conditions depend on each bank.
SIM-5.try: Try changing inflation to the low scenario (1,5 %) and see which one ends with more.
assumptions: The UVA is approximated with the scenario's inflation; the real UVA adjusts by CER with a lag.
The UVA minimum term and early withdrawal depend on the bank: check its conditions.
No taxes.

SIM-6.title: Interest-free installments or cash
SIM-6.short: Which is better in a scenario: a discount today or installments that inflation shrinks.
SIM-6.intro: Compare the discounted cash price with today's value of the installments, with the scenario's inflation.

price.label: Installment price
price.help: Total amount in pesos, for example: 120.000

inflation.label: Scenario monthly inflation
inflation.help: As a monthly percentage, for example: 3

first.label: First installment
first.help: Whether it is paid in a month or at the time of purchase.

SIM-6.main: In this scenario, the better option is
SIM-6.sentenceCash: Discounted cash ({{cash}}) costs less than today's value of the {{count}} installments of {{installment}} ({{pv}}).
SIM-6.sentenceInstallments: The {{count}} installments of {{installment}} are worth {{pv}} today, less than discounted cash ({{cash}}): inflation shrinks each installment.
SIM-6.chartTitle: What you pay, in today's pesos
SIM-6.chartCash: Cash is the lowest bar in this scenario.
SIM-6.chartInstallments: Today's value of the installments is the lowest bar in this scenario.
SIM-6.meaning: A future installment is worth less than the same amount today, because inflation raises prices. That is why interest-free installments can be better, unless the cash discount is bigger.
SIM-6.try: Try changing the discount to 5 % and see if the better option changes.
assumptions: Constant monthly inflation.
Equal, interest-free installments.
It does not include the yield you could get with the money.

SIM-7.title: Credit card
SIM-7.short: What paying the minimum costs compared with paying the total.
SIM-7.intro: See how long it takes and how much interest you pay if you only pay the minimum, with no new purchases.

tna.label: Financing rate (TNA)
tna.help: As an annual percentage, for example: 60

cft.label: Total financial cost (CFT)
cft.help: The one shown on your statement, as an annual percentage. For example: 95

minimum.label: Minimum payment
minimum.help: As a percentage of the balance, for example: 10

SIM-7.main: Interest if you pay the minimum
SIM-7.sentence_one: Paying the minimum, it takes you {{count}} month, you pay {{interest}} in interest and {{total}} in total. Paying the total today, you pay {{balance}}.
SIM-7.sentence_other: Paying the minimum, it takes you {{count}} months, you pay {{interest}} in interest and {{total}} in total. Paying the total today, you pay {{balance}}.
SIM-7.sentenceNever: With this data, the minimum payment does not cover the interest: the debt never gets paid off.
SIM-7.chartConclusion_one: The balance reaches zero in {{count}} month.
SIM-7.chartConclusion_other: The balance reaches zero in {{count}} months.
SIM-7.meaning: What you do not pay on the statement is financed at the card's rate. The CFT adds fees and charges to that rate: it is the number to compare. Paying the total avoids interest.
SIM-7.try: Try changing the minimum payment from 10 % to 5 % and see how many more months it takes.
assumptions: No new purchases or taxes: it is a simplification.
Monthly interest = TNA × 30 ÷ 365 on the balance; minimum with a floor of $ 1.000.
The CFT is shown for comparison; the calculation uses the TNA.

SIM-8.title: Savings goal with inflation
SIM-8.short: What your goal will cost and how much to set aside per month.
SIM-8.intro: Adjust your goal's price for the scenario's inflation and calculate how much to set aside each month.

inflation.label: Scenario monthly inflation
inflation.help: As a monthly percentage, for example: 3

return.label: Monthly yield on savings
return.help: As a monthly percentage; 0 if you keep it with no yield. For example: 2,5

SIM-8.sentence_one: What costs {{price}} today would cost {{future}} in {{count}} month. To get there, set aside {{monthly}} per month.
SIM-8.sentence_other: What costs {{price}} today would cost {{future}} in {{count}} months. To get there, set aside {{monthly}} per month.
SIM-8.chartTitle: Your goal's price and your savings
SIM-8.chartConclusion_one: The two lines meet in month {{count}}.
SIM-8.chartConclusion_other: The two lines meet in month {{count}}.
SIM-8.meaning: With inflation, a goal moves away if it is not adjusted. Calculating the final price and the monthly savings keeps you from arriving with less than you need.
SIM-8.try: Try adding a 2,5 % monthly yield and see how much the monthly savings drop.
assumptions: Constant monthly inflation and yield.
Equal contributions at the end of each month.

SIM-9.title: Getting out of debt: snowball or avalanche
SIM-9.short: Two ways to order your debts, compared side by side.
SIM-9.intro: Compare paying the smallest debt first (snowball) or the highest-rate one first (avalanche), with the same monthly amount.

r1.label: Debt 1 · annual rate
r1.help: As an annual percentage, for example: 150

m1.label: Debt 1 · minimum payment
m1.help: Amount in pesos per month, for example: 4.000

r2.label: Debt 2 · annual rate
r2.help: As an annual percentage, for example: 110

m2.label: Debt 2 · minimum payment
m2.help: Amount in pesos per month, for example: 1.500

r3.label: Debt 3 · annual rate
r3.help: As an annual percentage, for example: 80

m3.label: Debt 3 · minimum payment
m3.help: Amount in pesos per month, for example: 10.000

extra.label: Extra amount per month
extra.help: What you can add on top of the minimums, for example: 20.000

SIM-9.sentence_one: The avalanche saves you {{saving}} in interest; the snowball pays off the first debt {{count}} month sooner.
SIM-9.sentence_other: The avalanche saves you {{saving}} in interest; the snowball pays off the first debt {{count}} months sooner.
SIM-9.chartConclusion: The lowest bar is the one that pays the least interest.
SIM-9.order: Order in which they are paid off
SIM-9.meaning: The snowball tackles the smallest debt first and gives quick results; the avalanche tackles the highest rate first and pays less interest. What matters is paying all the minimums and keeping up the extra.
SIM-9.try: Try raising the extra amount to 40.000 and see how many fewer months it takes.
assumptions: Monthly interest = annual rate × 30 ÷ 365 on each balance.
When a debt is paid off, its minimum is added to the next one's payment.
The example data comes from the workshop presentation; the minimums and the extra are assumptions for practice.

SIM-10.title: Compound interest and regular contributions
SIM-10.short: How much a monthly contribution grows over time.
SIM-10.intro: See how capital grows with monthly contributions and an example annual rate.

rate.label: Expected annual rate
rate.help: As an annual percentage, for example: 12

SIM-10.sentence_one: Contributing {{monthly}} per month at {{rate}} a year for {{count}} year, you would reach {{final}} in this scenario; {{interest}} would be interest.
SIM-10.sentence_other: Contributing {{monthly}} per month at {{rate}} a year for {{count}} years, you would reach {{final}} in this scenario; {{interest}} would be interest.
SIM-10.chartConclusion: The gap between the two areas is the interest: it grows more the more time passes.
SIM-10.meaning: Compound interest makes interest earn interest too. That is why starting earlier weighs more than contributing a lot later. Past returns do not guarantee future returns.
SIM-10.try: Try lowering the years from 33 to 20 and see how much the result changes.
assumptions: Constant annual rate, monthly compounding (rate ÷ 12).
Contributions at the end of each month.
No taxes, fees or inflation. Past returns do not guarantee future returns.

SIM-11.title: CEDEAR: from the stock to the peso price
SIM-11.short: How a CEDEAR's price is formed and what moves it.
SIM-11.intro: Calculate a CEDEAR's theoretical price from the dollar price, the ratio and the implied exchange rate. All values are examples.

usdPrice.label: Stock or ETF price in dollars

ratio.label: Conversion ratio
ratio.help: How many CEDEARs equal one share. For example: 20 (20:1)

SIM-11.sentence: With a price of {{usd}}, a ratio of {{ratio}}:1 and an exchange rate of {{fx}}, the CEDEAR would be worth about {{price}}.
SIM-11.chartTitle: What happens if the stock or the exchange rate goes up 10 %
SIM-11.chartConclusion: Either increase moves the peso price in the same proportion.
SIM-11.meaning: A CEDEAR's price depends on the asset's price abroad and on the exchange rate. The real price can have a premium or a discount from supply and demand. Ratios can change: check the current list.
SIM-11.try: Try changing the ratio from 20 to 10 and see how each CEDEAR's price changes.
assumptions: Theoretical price: dollars ÷ ratio × implied exchange rate.
No fees or market charges.
The ratio is an example: current ones are on BYMA's list.

SIM-12.title: Where do I keep my emergency fund?
SIM-12.short: Compare liquidity, yield and protection of three options.
SIM-12.intro: Compare an interest-bearing account, a term deposit and a money market fund with example rates. It is not a recommendation: it is a comparison of features.

inflation.label: Scenario monthly inflation
inflation.help: As a monthly percentage, for example: 3

remunerated.help: Example value, as an annual percentage

fixedTerm.help: Example value, as an annual percentage

moneyMarket.help: Example value, as an annual percentage

hero.eyebrow: Alcancía design system · customized Material Design 3
hero.title: A calm system to talk about money without fear
hero.intro: The tokens, components and patterns the personal finance simulator is built with. Everything you see here is the product's real code: colors and contrasts are read live from the tokens.

principles.title: Six ideas that decide every screen
principles.intro: When two design options are valid, the one that best meets these principles wins.

tokens.title: Four tiers, no loose values
tokens.intro: Following Material Design 3 and the W3C Design Tokens Community Group: raw values live only in the first tier and every component uses named roles.

color.title: Trustworthy, clear and calm
color.intro: Indigo and teal over cool gray neutrals. No casino or trading look: color informs, it does not push you to decide.

type.title: Inter with the Material 3 scale
type.intro: Headings with the emphasized variant of M3 Expressive. Amounts, percentages and dates always with tabular figures, so they can be compared in a column.

space.title: An 8 px rhythm and tonal depth
space.intro: Airier in the learning views and denser in the dashboards. Depth comes from the surface, not from shadow.

icons.title: Material Symbols Rounded, weight 300
icons.intro: A single component, each icon imported as SVG. Outline by default and fill only for what is active.

motion.title: Short, meaningful and optional
motion.intro: 150 to 300 ms with the M3 curves. Each animation explains a change; none is looping decoration.

components.title: The product's real components
components.intro: None of these samples is an image: they are the same components the wallet and dashboards use, with their texts.

fuerte.title: The wallet's companion
fuerte.intro: The orange safe from the workshop's escape room keeps each person company: it welcomes them, warns them and celebrates with them. It is the only exception to the cool palette (D-52).

patterns.title: Solutions that repeat
patterns.intro: Each pattern carries the number of the decision that started it, recorded in docs/decisions.md.

money.title: Amounts that read well, compare well and do not scare
money.intro: The format, color and notices of each figure. We teach with scenarios, never with promises.

security.title: Privacy by design, in three layers
security.intro: What is simulated in the interface, what the front end really protects today and what a production version would add (D-70).

a11y.title: WCAG 2.2 AA from the design
a11y.intro: Standard ISO/IEC 40500:2025. Checked with axe on every screen and at 6 widths, with keyboard walkthroughs and a screen reader.

voice.title: Like someone who explains without judging
voice.intro: Neutral Latin American Spanish, with tú. Clear, patient and non-judgmental; never alarmist or salesy.

credits.title: What we did not make
credits.intro: Third-party resources, validated content and licenses.

hornero.title: The fictitious partner's brand
hornero.intro: Hornero is the fictitious wallet that shows Alcancía embedded in another app (D-75, D-84). It has its own brand built with tokens, does not refer to a real brand and is always labeled as a demo brand.

principles.title: Learn by using
principles.body: Participants do not enter a campus: they enter a wallet with fictitious money. Each action teaches something in the moment and sections open with achievements (D-50).

principles.title: Education, not advice
principles.body: Scenarios with their assumptions in view, never predictions. No screen recommends a product, an entity or an investment.

principles.title: Calm is not flat
principles.body: With no gradients and almost no shadows, richness comes from hierarchy, data, accent and layered composition.

principles.title: Privacy by design
principles.body: Amounts live only in each person's browser. The company sees aggregate learning, with a minimum of 5 people per group.

principles.title: For the office and the warehouse
principles.body: The same guide on Mariana's computer and on Diego's phone: short sessions, simple texts and nothing that depends on a gesture.

principles.title: Measured gamification
principles.body: Levels and achievements that celebrate healthy behaviors. No punishing streaks, no rankings, no countdowns or urgency.

rules: Notice types, in this order: attention, pending, your investments, goals and your progress. Each one with its container color and icon.

It shows the first three notices and "See N more notices" on the right. Each notice leads to the screen that resolves it.
In "Chatty", the visit's first new notice shows for a few seconds in a bubble next to it. "Only what matters" counts only attention ones.
With "Silent", the pending mission and the unpaid debit go back to the page.

designItems: The "Personal finance simulator · fictitious money" banner is on the whole wallet and is never removed (D-69).
The wallet does not imitate the colors, icons or flows of any real app.
It never asks for an ID, CBU, cards or passwords. The CVU is shown in a format that is not valid.
Amounts do not leave the browser

No figure is shown for groups of fewer than 5 people, and the admin cannot lower it.

a11y: Visible label, help with format and example, "(required)" in text and errors next to the field.
Everything works with the keyboard, focus is visible and never covered, and dialogs trap it.
Title, a sentence with the conclusion and the same information as a table.
